name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: We should add a two-layer focus ring: a 4px #005fcc outer ring with a 2px white inner ring on all interactive elements. This is the best option because it provides a clear visual indication of focus for users who rely on keyboard navigation, while also being visually distinct and consistent with our brand colors. By choosing this approach, we're accepting a minor trade-off in terms of added visual complexity, but it's a worthwhile compromise to ensure that our interface is usable by everyone. This decision also aligns with the Playwright MCP's emphasis on clear and consistent navigation cues.

name: Reader
text: The two-layer ring risks a muddy halo on patterned or dark backgrounds—#005fcc’s blue blends with busy textures, and the white inner ring loses crispness against dark surfaces. A single 4px ring with a white box-shadow (4px blur) keeps edges sharp on high-contrast backgrounds and meets WCAG 2.2 AA. Test it on a dark patterned page and a light one; if focus remains visible in both, it’s settled.

name: Ramp
text:
Adopt a single 4px #005fcc focus ring with a 2px white box-shadow blur on every focusable element. It stays crisp on both light and dark backgrounds, meets WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, and avoids the muddy halo risk of the two-layer ring. The trade-off is slightly less visual pop on patterned backgrounds, but that’s safer than the alternative.

name: Reader
text: The single 4px ring with white box-shadow still risks a fuzzy edge on high-contrast or patterned backgrounds—#005fcc’s blue can bleed into adjacent colors, and the blur may soften focus cues. A better alternative is a 3px #005fcc ring with a 1px white inset shadow, which sharpens edges without muddying halos. Test both on dark, light, and patterned backgrounds at 100% and 400% zoom to settle it.
